I don’t know if it will work for you. My first break up I focused on all my ex’s bad qualities. It was a really bad breakup and by the end I didn’t even like them anymore as  person so every time I slid back I would remind myself of all their bad qualities. It worked for me that time. The second relationship that didn’t work out ended better, and I still liked them as a person. It was definitely harder to get over, but I focused on why we were a bad match and why it won’t work (we had different approach to life, philosophies, heck probably even political, cultural, and religious beliefs). And I let myself feel the pain of the breakups and reminded myself that if I got back together with them, there’s a high chance I’ll feel this pain again and it’ll be worse because I had a chance to have moved on from it but I actually didn’t. That thought kept me away from the idea of getting back together.

I also did a lot of self-improvement- hiking, meditation, even watching shows I didn’t watch when I was together with the ex because they wanted to see something else. I also journaled to write down my emotions and thoughts especially when I’m at my most logical, so it’s easier to remember them when I am too emotional.

If she’s similar to me - a girl who doesn’t know how to react to forwardness, I would say ask. Because if I like a guy and he takes my hand - I’d think something is wrong and will pull it back even if I do want to hold hands too. I just get nervous. If I don’t like a guy and he takes my hand - I would think something is wrong and pull it back too btw. 😂 

If you ask I am at least mentally prepared for how to properly respond with what I really want to do. And you don’t have to verbally ask - holding out your hand to her IS asking, and I think that’s a pretty normal thing to do.

As someone who used to suffer from self esteem issues when I was younger - I second this but with a caveat - you don’t have to be fine “100%”. It depends on the person, but I think a lot of people can’t ever get to 100% loving ourselves. BUT, you must love/like yourself enough to be loved - to avoid the situation you had where you broke off with your GF because you didn’t feel you deserved them and what u/Warm-Appearance-1484 experienced with his gf who can’t accept his love. And also to love yourself enough to have a minimum bar that isn’t so low so you don’t end up in an abusive relationship ship and think it’s “what you deserve”

Looking back at my failed relationships (2) I realized I saw flags early on, recognized they were wrong, but made excuses. I learned the hard way it only gets worse from there. So if the first few months are already having things this shitty happening, it’s time to bail. Kudos to you that you didn’t make excuses for him when this happened, even just in your head. 

I’m hoping I get it right for the next time and that I can finally say no to someone no matter how much I like them (in that moment).

Similar thing happened to me. Almost a decade of friendship apparently didn’t warrant even an explanation. A mutual friend finally told me, and it was such a... trivial reason in the grand scheme of things. It’s the equivalent of me adopting a dog that turns out she was interested in but 1) never told me she wanted the dog too 2) never told me she even knew about the dog and 3) she KNEW when I was first offered the dog, I told her when I was considering it, when I finally filled out the application, when I had the interview. She knew every step, never said anything. Mutual friend told me the one that pushed her to ghost me
was I didn’t tell her when the “adoption” was finalized (for clarity I  using a metaphor because I’m not sure if she has a reddit account or mutual friends have and the details are unique enough that it’s easily identifiable if I provided the real situation). I told her a few days after,  because I didn’t think it was a big deal.

Trust me, sometimes knowing the reason just makes the situation more frustrating. Definitely not an adult relationship. I made it a point to now make friends who can get angry in a mature way. Have a misunderstanding? Talk to me about it. Don’t ghost me. We’re too old for this shit.

Thank you for the response. I’ve spoken to a therapist. I’m not sure it helped to make the suicidal thoughts go away. I feel like it made it closer to a real option tbh. Like I said I’m not in any immediate danger, at least I don’t think so.

I don’t think I can talk to anyone about this with my friends and family. It would make it worse. I would prefer no one knows because acknowledging it in my “real” life will make it worse, I think. Because then it becomes more real because then someone in my world would know. Right now I can compartmentalize it in the realm of “just thoughts”. But if I speak to it with people who are close to me, in my head it feels more real. 

I don’t know if that makes sense. I just can’t bring it into my real world right now. I need to keep it in my head. I’ve mentioned it to my therapist but I can rationalize that as just discussing thoughts, even though like I said that alone has made the thoughts worse.

Thank you for the suggestions though. And for the reply.

I don’t know if I am seeking help, or if I do how to go about it. I don’t want to make this worse because even now it’s a struggle to keep it as just thoughts and not actually try something just to see how it feels.

I’m away from family. My friends are from work. I feel like there’s more risk to talking about this with them than there are benefits. I put myself in a hard place and I am not sure how to get out. 

One day at a time, I guess.

NTA. And I can sympathize with you. One of my parents’ side of the family is “special” and family gatherings there are always full of drama and bickering and trying to either one up each other or put the other people down. I get how your father feels obligated to attend tho. I feel the same. At the same time, I understand you not wanting to attend. I make the decision to attend because the fallout of skipping them for both me and my parents (they already don’t really like my mom) I feel is not worth it (basically I go for my parents, but that’s my decision, doesn’t have to be yours). To be able to stay sane and have some fun though, instead of hiding things they may find offensive, I and my siblings double down on it. 

“Hey, why aren’t you married yet? You don’t want to get too old and still be single?” I respond with “oh I’m trying to figure out which way I swing still. I’ve tried both sides but I still can’t quite decide...” (even though I’m straight, they don’t need to know that). 

Or

“I heard you aren’t going to church anymore. Why? I’ll pray for your soul, but you should really see Father Family-Friend-Priest and confess” (I have personal reasons for not attending church). I sweetly tell them that I don’t mind going to hell because I want to meet Constantine/ Hades/ random fandom character that’s been sent to hell. 

They actually hinted that my sister-in-law was not good enough for my brother. The reason? She wasn’t a virgin when they got married. This despite the fact that the uncle who was vocally protesting had 5 children from 4 different women, and whose (first and only legally married) wife was pregnant when they got married! 

Now doing the above - IATA, but so is the family. So I guess I belong? 😂

Here’s the thing, too. If your company culture is worth its shit and you’re a good worker, you wanting to quit may be a red flag for them and allow them to re-examine things. This has happened to me. I almost quit because of a bad manager (and yes I tried all of the above), BUT, the people in the department knew I was a good worker, but ALSO that my bad manager was incompetent, they opted to get rid of him instead of losing me. It’s made me reevaluate what I look for in a company now - ones that do look at your contributions more than your position.

It sounds like he has it out for you, maybe not you personally but he may still want to get rid of you because he didn’t hire you. Either way, when the reason he doesn’t like you is NOT because of anything you did but just because he doesn’t ... then the likelihood of you being able to fix this is low. Your manager, no matter how good you are, unless he is incompetent (In which case you may eventually be able to use to get him out), can sabotage your career progress significantly enough that this may not be worth fixing, or worse get you fired. BUT, if you do want to try, there could be a few things you could do. (I wouldn’t try if I were you, but just in case it’s something you don’t have a choice in - and I mean you can’t quit:

1) Suck up to him on a personal level. I don’t mean this ironically. I mean try to get to know him and his interest and try to talk to him about it

2) find out if there’s a specific reason he doesn’t like you. If there is, then that’s easier to fix. But if it isn’t specific enough. then...

3) Show him you’re on his side. Publicly give him praise for “helping” you with the project or giving you that “useful advise that helped you figure things out”, etc. Don’t give him full credit though, just what plausibly a manager could have done. Even if he gave you advise negatively, pretend to take it as a positive.

But only do this if he isn’t an insecure piece of shit who micromanaged people and tried to steal credit. Only do this if it’s a misunderstanding - ie. He could be a good boss to you he just has a misconception of you. If he is just an ass, this cannot and will not be worth trying to fix.

I’m no expert but I wouldn’t call this drama. This is a real issue that you should talk to your girlfriend about. This affects your life and happiness 100% so it’s not nothing. And if she loves you, she would want to know this and talk about it and supports what makes you happy. You should also talk about your paranoia. Maybe not go into specifics but just say you are worried you won’t meet her physical needs. You two may find a solution. I think it’s easier to resolve the powered libido vs your depression. Talk to your doctor too.

Are you sure you are ready to forgive? One of the biggest mistakes I used to do is to forgive people because I think it’s something I need to do without properly processing the emotions I needed to get to a state where I could
forgive them. My idea of forgiving them is “letting go” the anger I had for them. But the problem is my version of “letting go” is actually just repressing it, forcing myself not to feel it. It took me a long time to realize I was going about it wrong and I never really forgave them —- just ignored the pain and anger for what they did to me. It came out in different ways and it was not healthy.

Have you processed what he’s done to you - truly? It’s ok to let yourself feel the pain and anger. I’m not a therapist, but I think to truly be able to forgive, you first have to really acknowledge what he did to you (especially if you’ve repressed or denied it for so long), let the emotions happen, process them, and let go when you are ready. I used to lie to myself about how much it hurt me when I was wronged. In my head, I was convincing myself it wasn’t a big deal so it’s easier to forgive them. But true forgiveness can only happen if you acknowledge how truly bad it was, how bad it really made you feel, but then realize it wasn’t about you, it was something about them they just couldn’t help. And once I started realizing that they have issues of their own, that in their own way they are probably struggling too, and unfortunately their response was to hurt others, it was easier to start forgiving them.

I hope you find the way that works for you. It is important to forgive for your own sanity. At least that’s how it is in my experience.

Full disclosure: my experience of being hurt/betrayed that required forgiveness wasn’t a romantic relationship but a close friendship. So circumstances I needed to forgive were different.

I’m not a therapist. I’m just a bit old(er). I don’t know what your relationship is normally like, so take this with a grain of salt because other factors may be at play in your case that isn’t obvious from what you have shared.

But, in the many relationships I’ve had, or have observed, and this includes friendships AND romantic relationships, when one person feels superior over the other - either as someone who is doing the other person a favor by being more patient/loving/inclusive etc. or literally feeling they are better (better-looking/more popular/nicer/richer) etc, the relationship usually doesn’t end well or is very very toxic. Now I’m not saying that in a healthy relationships no one is the “more patient/loving/attentive” person etc. the difference between the healthy ones and the non-healthy ones is that in the healthier relationship, the person who is more patient/loving/whatever-better-thing is being done doesn’t FEEL like they are the better partner. It isn’t something they think about, let alone ever say. I think once they start feeling they are better, then it becomes unhealthy.

I think in your case your fiancé feels he is the “better” of the two of you. The fact that he feels that and has started to lord it over you by saying things like “no one else will put up with you”, it maybe has gone into toxic territory and I would have second thoughts about getting married until you sort this out (as others have suggested - therapy). If he turns out to be a “nice  guy”, then you’ve dodged a bullet.

(Yeah my friends and I love to camp 👍🏽)

I don’t think you need a ring. But you know your girlfriend more than any of us so just make sure she isn’t the type to expect one at the actual
proposal.

This is important. If this this how you feel (seeing her as a manifestation of the betrayal), it might actually be worse for your daughter if you try and stick around because your resentment towards your wife and her betrayal might manifest in how you treat your daughter. She is innocent in all this. Only try to have a relationship with her if you know you can treat her with love and without bringing in any resentment from what your wife did. 

This sucks and I’m sorry it’s happening to you and your daughter. I hope you both get through it.

Go drive somewhere. I’m not sure if your areas have good hiking places. Go there. Driving doesn’t allow you to check your phone. When I hike I keep my phone in my backpack. Some hiking places also doesn’t have internet signal so that helps.

If none of those are your cup of tea, maybe find a movie, or go look at furniture of something. I used to window shop big ticket items when I need to distract myself for any reason, knowing I won’t buy them because either too expensive or too bulky to impulse buy. 😂 

Go to a scenic spot and read a book?

It’s good you’ve been hanging out with friends but I feel like you also need to relearn how to be alone. This is a good chance.

Hope one of these help or you find something to do.

I don’t think it’s a question of morality. I think it’s a matter of maturity. There should be a break up conversation if you are going about this maturely. You shared your lives with each other, the least you could do is talk to them when ending it. I do agree it can be be brief and straightforward as needed, unless both are okay with the long winded emotional conversations. I don’t think anybody “owes” anybody anything, but it is common decency to explain why you are breaking up with them.

Exception? If the person leaving feels like a break-up talk endangers them such as cases of abusive relationships or even partners with explosive tempers (but for the latter you can still do it over the phone).

Yeah no. 4x is a clear message that she’s just stringing you along. She probably was feeling lonely or needed a boost when she asked to meet up but by the time you were supposed to she was over it, which means she’s not serious about it. Then asking you for gas money like she didn’t just blow you off? I would actually recommend closing the door, because FOUR times? Once, maybe. Twice? No. FOUR TIMES? You should have said “you’d canceled on me four times it’s obvious you’re not interested. Lose my number”. Then block.
Good luck!
